slice: Pipeline Run 7 / Slice 7C - Tauri desktop icon family

raster.png: 8-bit RGBA, rounded-plate corners transparent outside the rx=7 plate

alpha_check.method: ImageMagick pixel sampling: RGBA values read at the four canvas corners, the image center and a plate-only left-mid pixel for every standalone PNG and for every PNG payload extracted from the ICO and ICNS containers.
alpha_check.expectation: corners fully transparent because the plate is rounded (the four standalone PNGs measure alpha=0 exactly; the 16 px container payload shows up to 12/255 residual alpha from Chromium sub-pixel antialiasing of the rx=7 arc, not a background fill; tolerance 0.05); plate pixels fully opaque #09090b (srgba(9,9,11,1)); image center exposes the plate through the mark's visor cutout.

svg_checks.tokens_expected: <rect width="32" height="32" rx="7" fill="#09090b"/> present: True

svg_vector_parity.method: Chromium renders icon.svg inline at 1024x1024 (device_scale_factor=1, omit_background=True) and the screenshot is compared byte-for-byte with icon.png

validation_sheet.background: #18181b dark (slightly lighter than the #09090b plate so the rounded plate silhouette is visible)

inspection.observations: Contact sheet inspected: row 1 shows icon.png at 1024 px, the icon.icns ic14 payload at 512 px, 128x128@2x.png at 256 px, 128x128.png at 128 px and 32x32.png at 32 px, all native size; row 2 shows an 8x nearest-neighbour zoom of the 32 px render and a 2x nearest-neighbour zoom of the 128 px render. Every render shows the same Visor Hutch master mark (#34d399) on the opaque #09090b rounded plate (rx=7) with transparent corners outside the plate, and the #18181b sheet background makes the rounded plate silhouette visible. No white corner blocks, no legacy hexagon mark, no clipping or colour drift; labels are legible and do not overlap.

commands: cmp -s <generated file> <staged file>  # for each of the 7 staged files
identify -format '%wx%h %[channels]' <generated/staged PNGs and extracted container payloads>
python3: struct-parse icon.ico (count/sizes/offsets/bit counts) and icon.icns (magic/total length/type codes/lengths/PNG magic/IHDR dims)
Chromium icon.svg -> 1024 px render, byte-compared with icon.png (single-vector parity)

environment.imagemagick: Version: ImageMagick 7.1.2-34 Q16-HDRI x86_64 c5d4ca8a0:20261014 https://imagemagick.org
environment.renderer: Playwright headless Chromium, device_scale_factor=1, exact viewport

decision_note: A-vs-B/C omit_background decision: the four plated PNGs are rendered with omit_background=True (Option A). The original task wording said 'opaque plate (omit_background=False)'; with the reference recipe (transparent page body) Chromium fills the area outside the rx=7 plate with white at omit_background=False (Option B), producing white corner blocks, and a variation that sets an opaque #09090b page background (Option C) loses the rounded-plate silhouette. Lead confirmed Option A: Tauri/deb/AppImage/macOS app-icon conventions expect the opaque rounded plate as the shape with transparency outside it, and the approved production/icons/icon-512.png was itself rendered with omit_background=True (byte parity proof below). All plate pixels remain fully opaque #09090b and every PNG is 8-bit RGBA.
u07_resolution: U07 (desktop icon family drift) is closed at source and raster level. The four legacy files (icon.svg/icon.png/icon.ico/icon.icns) used an undocumented pointy-top hexagon mark: #28cd9d stroke on a #0f151e rounded plate, geometry differing from every documented Hutch mark. They are now replaced by the maintainer-approved 'Visor Hutch' master mark (hutch-mark-master.svg, #34d399, fill-rule evenodd) centred on the documented full-bleed #09090b rx=7 plate - the exact composition already used by production/icons/icon-512.png. Seven files are generated deterministically into .pipeline/brand/2026-10/assets/production/desktop/ (32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png, icon.png, icon.ico, icon.icns, icon.svg) and staged byte-identically into desktop/icons/; icon.svg is now a 1024x1024 single-vector source (viewBox 0 0 32 32) that matches the rasters, and the ICNS ic14 512 px payload is byte-identical to the approved icon-512.png (sha256 ce3da0b9be7a4ee66a168f639cc854d3493cc2f132e43a7c3120756ae5226af5), so the desktop host no longer carries a divergent mark variant. desktop/tauri.bundle.conf.json is intentionally unchanged (it lists only icons/icon.png, icons/icon.ico, icons/icon.icns).
caveats: ImageMagick 7 in this environment has no ICNS decode delegate, so icon.icns is validated by byte-level Python parsing plus PNG payload extraction/IHDR/alpha checks, not by identify(1) on the .icns file itself.

PNG bytes are Chromium-build dependent; determinism is guaranteed for a fixed toolchain (versions recorded in environment) and was verified by two consecutive generator runs with identical sha256 for all 7 outputs.

The staged Tauri-convention PNGs 32x32.png, 128x128.png and 128x128@2x.png are not referenced by desktop/tauri.bundle.conf.json (which lists only icon.png/icon.ico/icon.icns); the config was left unchanged as required.
Legacy desktop/icons/ files were replaced in the working tree; they remain tracked so the maintainer can review/revert via git (no commit was made).
